capitals.note: "The article says the tribe's capital is Merowe" (not the archaeological site of Meroe). Coordinates approximate.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria lacks the Shaigiya). The map caption: Dar Shaigiya in 1820 extends "from Korti in the south to Berti Island in the north"; the page has no area. A 170 km radius round Dongola covers the reach; the Funj dossier (af-01-b) has the Shaigiya taking Dongola from the Funj in 1782, the page here has the break from the Funj around 1690.

ledger.note: c. 1690: the Shaiqiya break from the Funj. "Around 1690 the tribe broke loose from the Kingdom of Funj, defeating the Abdelab governor", becoming "the region's only independent tribe".

region.text: Dar Shaigiya, "from Korti in the south to Berti Island in the north"

ledger.note: 4 November 1820: the Shaiqiya are beaten at Korti. "Egyptian firearms and artillery defeated the Shaygiya cavalry" (4 November) and destroyed their infantry on Jebel Daiqa on 2 December; their leader Mac Jaweesh fled to Shendi (Shaiqiya page).

region.text: Dar Shaigiya, "from Korti in the south to Berti Island in the north"

ledger.note: November 1820: the independent Shaigiya end; they serve the Turkish army and are rewarded with Ja'alin land between Shendi and Khartoum after 1822.

wars.outcome: Egyptian victory at Korti on 4 November 1820 and Jebel Daiqa on 2 December 1820; the Shaiqiya submit and serve the Turks.
wars.note: The Shaiqiya had been challenged at Dongola around 1811 (Shaiqiya page).

certainty.note: A river kingdom described by its two ends, Korti and Berti Island.

sources.title: Shaiqiya
sources.note: Dar Shaigiya: independent after 1365, Funj subjects by 1523, broke loose c. 1690, extent Korti to Berti Island, capital Merowe, defeated at Korti in 1820, service to the Turks, Mahdist War 1884.

notes: New dossier: Cliopatria lacks the Shaigiya. Pages opened: Shaiqiya, Turco-Egyptian conquest of Sudan (2). The funj-sultanate dossier (af-01-b) has the Shaigiya take Dongola in 1782; this page has Dar Shaigiya independent c. 1690 (it was part of Makuria, independent after 1365, then Funj subject by 1523). The counterpart string 'Shaigiya (Shaykiyya)' of the Funj dossier equals this slug. Later: Shaiqiya served the Turks against the Ja'alin in 1822 and received their lands between Shendi and Khartoum; in April 1884 Saleh Bey and 1,400 men surrendered to the Mahdi. Gazetteer names needed: Korti, Berti Island, Merowe (Marawi). Capital coordinate approximate.
